newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Colombian rebels seek Venezuelan talks -report.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels seek Venezuelan talks -report.

text.p: Colombia's largest rebel group, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), wants to open talks with Venezuela to reduce growing violence on the border, a rebel spokesman was quoted on Wednesday as saying.
"We're ready to present ourselves to the Venezuelan government to begin the necessary dialogue," El Universal newspaper quoted FARC international spokesman Commander Ariel as saying.
"Venezuela can't be the enemy of a guerrilla group that is offering a way out from what is happening on its border," he said.

Ariel distanced the FARC from a spate of recent cross-border incursions by another Colombian guerrilla group, the National Liberation Army (ELN), that have strained relations between the two countries and prompted Venezuelan calls for a multinational border peace-keeping force.

Local politicians often invoke the specter of Colombian instability spreading across the 1,400-mile (2,200-km) frontier, along which kidnapping, smuggling and drug trafficking have increased in recent years.
